alternating-a-b-week-school-timetable-ca.title: Alternating Week A / Week B School Timetable on a Calendar: Handling Vacation Breaks
alternating-a-b-week-school-timetable-ca.short: Week A / Week B Timetable & Holidays
alternating-a-b-week-school-timetable-ca.description: Set up an alternating Week A / Week B school or college schedule (`INTERVAL=2`) and handle 1-week school breaks whether they keep or flip Week A/B parity.
alternating-a-b-week-school-timetable-ca.lede: Setting up a two-week alternating school, college, or teaching timetable (`Week A` and `Week B`) is simple at the start of term: Week A classes repeat every 2 weeks (`INTERVAL=2`) from Week 1, and Week B classes repeat every 2 weeks from Week 2. The moment a 1-week half-term or Thanksgiving break arrives, however, schools split into two opposite rules—**Calendar-Locked A/B Weeks** vs **Pause-and-Resume A/B Weeks**—and using the wrong calendar edit will put every class after the break onto the wrong week!
alternating-a-b-week-school-timetable-ca.commonBelief: Deleting the classes during a 1-week school break automatically shifts Week B to the week after the holiday.

sections.heading: How the base 2-week Week A / Week B timetable maps to `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2`
body: In a 10-day (`two-week`) academic timetable, `Week A` (Monday–Friday of odd term weeks) and `Week B` (Monday–Friday of even term weeks) have different class periods, lab blocks, or teaching rooms. In iCalendar (RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10), Microsoft Outlook (`Recurrence -> Weekly -> Recur every 2 week(s)`), and Google Calendar (`Does not repeat` -> choose how often the event repeats and when it ends), you build the timetable with two sets of recurring events:
- **Week A Series:** Created during the first week of term (`Term Week 1`) repeating every 2 weeks (`RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=...`).
- **Week B Series:** Created during the second week of term (`Term Week 2`) repeating every 2 weeks (`RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=...`).

Adding an all-day transparent (`Show as: Free`) header event on Monday–Friday of each week titled **`[WEEK A]`** and **`[WEEK B]`** lets students, teachers, and parents see at a glance which timetable week is active in Month and Week views.

sections.heading: The crucial holiday question: Does a 1-week break keep parity or flip parity?
body: Before you edit a single vacation week on your calendar, check your school's official academic calendar for the week immediately **after** a 1-week break (note: a **2-week break** is 14 days = an even number of weeks, so both systems stay aligned after a 2-week break! A **1-week break** or **3-week break** is an odd number of weeks, where the two systems diverge):

- **Model 1 — Calendar-Locked Parity (Holiday Replaces the Scheduled Week):** Each calendar week of the year is pre-assigned as A or B. If Week 3 is `Week A`, Week 4 is a 1-week Vacation (which *would* have been `Week B`), and Week 5 resumes as **`Week A`**, then the odd/even calendar cadence never changed! Under RFC 5545 Section 3.8.5.1 (`EXDATE`), excluding the classes on Week 4 (or deleting those single vacation occurrences in your calendar app) leaves Week 5 as `Week A` automatically.

- **Model 2 — Instructional-Week Pause-and-Resume (Holiday Pauses the Cycle and Flips Parity):** Only active teaching weeks count. If Week 3 is `Week A`, Week 4 is a 1-week Vacation, and the school resumes in Week 5 with **`Week B`** (pushing every subsequent A and B week forward by 7 days), simply deleting Week 4's occurrences (`EXDATE`) will **fail**—because an `INTERVAL=2` rule still puts `Week A` on Week 5!

sections.heading: Illustrative 8-week term table comparing Model 1 (`EXDATE`) vs Model 2 (`UNTIL` + Parity Flip)
body: Consider an illustrative 8-week autumn term segment running **Monday, November 2 through Friday, December 25, 2026**, with a **1-week break in Calendar Week 4 (Monday, November 23 – Friday, November 27, 2026)**. Compare how Model 1 and Model 2 assign `Week A` and `Week B` in Weeks 5–8 (`Nov 30 – Dec 25, 2026`), and see the exact calendar actions required for each model.

sections.heading: How to set up Model 2 (Parity Flip) without creating mid-term editing messes
body: If your school uses **Model 2 (Pause-and-Resume)** where a 1-week break flips odd/even weeks for the next half-term, never create a single `INTERVAL=2` series spanning the entire September-to-June school year.
Instead, **bound each half-term block with its own `UNTIL` end date (`Last Friday Before Break`)** when you first enter the timetable:
- **Half-Term 1 (`Nov 2 – Nov 20, 2026`):** `Week A` starts `Mon Nov 2` (ending `Fri Nov 20`); `Week B` starts `Mon Nov 9` (ending `Fri Nov 20`).
- **Vacation Week (`Nov 23 – Nov 27, 2026`):** Zero classes generated automatically (`No EXDATE deletions needed!`).

- **Half-Term 2 (`Nov 30 – Dec 18, 2026`):** Create the post-break `Week B` series starting `Mon Nov 30` (ending `Fri Dec 18`) and the `Week A` series starting `Mon Dec 7` (ending `Fri Dec 18`). Bounding each half-term with `UNTIL` takes less than a minute and guarantees that a 1-week holiday never puts the rest of the semester on the wrong week.

comparison.heading: Illustrative 8-Week School Term Comparison: Calendar-Locked (Model 1) vs Pause-and-Resume (Model 2) Across a 1-Week Break

practical: Check your school's printed term calendar for the Monday **immediately after** each 1-week break before creating your recurring series: if the week before a 1-week break is `Week A` and the week after the break is `Week B`, your school uses **Model 2 (Pause-and-Resume)**.
For **Model 1 (Calendar-Locked)**, create 2-week (`INTERVAL=2`) series for the full term and simply delete single vacation occurrences (`EXDATE` in RFC 5545).

For **Model 2 (Pause-and-Resume)**, set the end date (`UNTIL`) of every recurring class to the **last Friday before each 1-week break**, and start a fresh half-term series on the Monday after the break.
Keep all timetable events in a dedicated `School Timetable` subcalendar so you can share it with family or hide it during summer vacation with a single tap.

faq.q: Why did deleting the classes during our 1-week school break leave the wrong Week A / Week B schedule for the rest of the semester?
faq.a: Because deleting a single week of occurrences (`EXDATE` in RFC 5545) only removes those dates—it does not shift the underlying 2-week (`INTERVAL=2`) cadence. If your school paused the rotation during the 1-week break so `Week B` moved to the week after the holiday, end the pre-break series on the Friday before the holiday (`UNTIL`) and start the post-break series on the Monday after the holiday.

faq.q: Why does a 2-week winter or spring break NOT flip Week A and Week B under either system?
faq.a: Because 2 weeks is `14 days`, which is an exact multiple of the 2-week (`14-day`) `INTERVAL=2` cycle. If the last teaching week before a 2-week break is `Week A`, skipping two calendar weeks lands naturally on `Week B` when school resumes.

faq.q: What if my school uses a 6-day or 10-day rotating Day 1–Day 6 schedule that skips weekends and holidays instead of Week A / Week B?
faq.a: A weekday-only `Day 1–Day 6` rotation changes weekdays every week and shifts by 1 day after every single Monday/Friday holiday; it is best entered either via your school portal's subscribed `.ics` calendar feed or by bounding short blocks between holidays.
